Install back-to-front (B2F) airflow fan trays (blue handles) and PSUs (blue release latches)' (dcs510-qsg/doc.md:116-120) - so this configuration is the same geometry in the blue skins.","kind":"orderable","part-numbers":{"9716-32D-O-A C-B-UK":{"part":"FP5ZZ8632301A","power-cord":"UK"},"9716-32D-O-AC-B-EU":{"part":"FP5ZZ8632201A","power-cord":"EU"},"9716-32D-O-AC-B-JP":{"part":"FP5ZZ8632501A","power-cord":"JP"},"9716-32D-O-AC-B-US":{"part":"FP5ZZ8632401A","power-cord":"N. America"}},"skins":{"fan-module-46":"blue","psu-ac-1300":"blue"}},"ac-f2b":{"airflow":"front-to-back","default":true,"description":"Dual 1300 W AC PSUs and six fan trays with front-to-back airflow, shipped with red release latches and red fan handles. This is a fixed 1RU switch, so the base configuration is the box as it is bought - supplies and fans populated, cages empty.","kind":"base","part-numbers":{"9716-32D-O-A C-F-UK":{"part":"FP5ZZ8632300A","power-cord":"UK"},"9716-32D-O-AC-F-EU":{"part":"FP5ZZ8632200A","power-cord":"EU"},"9716-32D-O-AC-F-JP":{"part":"FP5ZZ8632500A","power-cord":"JP"},"9716-32D-O-AC-F-US":{"part":"FP5ZZ8632400A","power-cord":"N. America"}}}},"description":"32x 400G QSFP-DD 1RU data-centre spine switch (vendor alias AS9716-32D), Broadcom Tomahawk 3 BCM56980, ONIE-preloaded. All ports on the front; two 1300 W AC PSUs and six 5+1 fan trays from the rear, in front-to-back and back-to-front airflow SKUs.","format":1,"gaps":[{"reason":"needs-photo","scope":["front"],"wanted":"A small mark sits between the Reset button and the ToD jack in dcs510-datasheet/fig-0007 and is unresolved at 3.3 px/mm. It could be the ToD port's own legend or an ESD-point symbol. Nothing is printed there rather than guess: the QSG's system-LED zoom (fig-0005) crops it away and the stock photographs are too small. A straight-on bench photograph of the left-hand end of the faceplate settles it.","what":"reset-area-legend"},{"reason":"needs-photo","scope":["front"],"wanted":"Every other port on this face carries printing and the ToD jack appears to as well, but no held image resolves it. Same photograph as above.","what":"tod-port-legend"},{"reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["rear"],"wanted":"Neither document gives a per-fan or per-tray figure; the only wattage either states is the chassis's own 1300 W maximum. Edgecore publishes no technical-specifications appendix for this model. L29 stands on common/fan-module@1 and the chassis module total is a floor.","what":"fan-tray-power-draw"},{"reason":"needs-photo","scope":["rear"],"wanted":"The quick-start's FRU list names 'Product label' as callout 4 (dcs510-qsg/doc.md:71) and dcs510-qsg/fig-0008 reproduces the barcode itself, but neither rear elevation resolves where on the face it is applied. Not drawn rather than placed by guess.","what":"rear-product-label-position"},{"reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["top","bottom","left","right"],"wanted":"Sized from the datasheet triple and given only what the stock three-quarter photograph supports - a lid seam, a rear vent strip and the side rail lines, all estimated. No mechanical drawing in the intake dimensions a single feature on these four faces.","what":"minor-face-geometry"}],"groups":{"fans":{"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"furniture":{"description":"the rack ears and the pull-out information tab - things you neither connect to nor read.","index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"grounding":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Point"},"leds":{"index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the management cluster at the right-hand end of the faceplate - the out-of-band 1000BASE-T RJ-45, the RS-232 console, two SFP+ 10G management uplinks and a USB-A service port. Four media, one job; the vendor draws them as one block under one legend and so do we.","role":"management","term":"Port"},"psus":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"2 pcs 1+1 redundant, load-sharing, hot-swappable 1200 W AC"},"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"qsfpdd-400g":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp-dd","speed":"400g"},"index-origin":1,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"},"qsfpdd-leds":{"index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"LED"},"timing":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the frequency and phase reference block at the left-hand end of the faceplate - 10 MHz IN/OUT and 1PPS IN/OUT on SMA, and Time-of-Day on a shielded RJ-45. Three media, one job: they synchronise this switch to an external clock and they are the only ports on the box that carry no data.","role":"management","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"Edgecore","maturity":"modelled","model":"DCS510","name":"dcs510","portfolio":{"family":"Ethernet Switch","line":"Data Center","series":"DCS510"},"provenance":{"cable-management":"the AC cord retainer bail visible on the PSU in dcs510-qsg/fig-0006 is not drawn - it is an accessory rather than a panel fact.","chassis":"datasheet - 'Dimensions (WxDxH): 43.84 x 53.6 x 4.31 cm' (dcs510-datasheet/doc.md:103), corroborated by the quick-start's hardware specification '438.4 x 536 x 43.1 mm (17.26 x 21.1 x 1.7 in.)' (dcs510-qsg/doc.md:234). 438.4 is already the BODY between the ear folds - it is not 482/19 in - so nothing is subtracted here; the rack ears are drawn as optional placements outside it, at the library's 14 mm.","chassis-colour":"photo - the chassis is black. The quick-start's line art (fig-0004, fig-0009) renders a light-grey shell, and it is the odd one out: the datasheet elevation, all three vendor stock photographs and the FRU photographs (fig-0006, fig-0007, fig-0013) show a black chassis with a silver PSU face. Where the guide art and the real device disagree the device wins.","cutouts":"every hole RESTATES the aperture its occupant already declares, rather than being measured a second time: position is the placement's own `at` plus the component's aperture offset, size is the registry entry the component `conforms:` to (or the component's own size where it conforms to nothing). The 32 port holes come out of expand.py that way. Three were hand-written around the visible opening with clearance instead - mgmt-eth at 14.4 x 10.4 where common/rj45-eth@1 is 15.8 x 13.2, and the two SFP+ cages at 15.0 x 9.2 where common/sfp-plus-cage@2 forwards to std/sfp's 14.5 x 10.0 at an offset of [0.75, 0] - and spec/tests/test_cutout_derivation.py failed on all three. They are now derived. The measured openings that produced those three numbers are still recorded in `management-cluster` above, and where they disagree with the part it is the PART that the drawing follows, because one fact recorded twice is a fact the drawing gets to be wrong about.","fan-numerals":"measured - each numeral sits on the chassis divider to the RIGHT of the tray it names, 6 to 1 left to right. The tray body reads 46.7 mm wide on a 48.8 mm pitch in dcs510-datasheet/fig-0007 panel 1, so the dividers are ~2.1 mm; the bays are drawn at 46.6 on that pitch and common/fan-module@1 (behaviour: fills) takes the bay's width rather than its own 48.6, which is what leaves the metal the numerals are printed on. It was drawn twice before that: at common/fan-module@1's own 48.6 the numerals were painted under their own trays and L21 said so on all six, and with the bay narrowed under the 48.6 generic L33 said the module was 2 mm wider than its opening. Both warnings were the drawing telling the truth about a part that is the sibling AS7726-32X's tray rather than this one's, so the tray got its own contract - common/fan-module-46@1, the same 44.6 mm square on a 2 mm mounting tab instead of a 4 mm one, which keeps the rotor round rather than scaling it to fit.","figure-choice":"Gate 1, from the prepared brief's ranked candidates. dcs510-qsg/fig-0004 panel 0, box [4,30,803,108], is orthographic to 0.7 percent (1.8225 px/mm on x, 1.8097 on y) and is the source of every VERTICAL number here, through the prepared band report. dcs510-datasheet/fig-0007 panel 0, box [8,124,1450,270], is NOT orthographic - 2.9 percent, its box 6 px too tall because the render's lower shadow is inside it - but its x scale (3.2892 px/mm) agrees to 0.3 percent with panel 1 of the same figure (3.2801), which IS orthographic, so its x is corroborated twice and it is the source of every HORIZONTAL number here. Where a y had to come off that figure it was mapped through the orthographic panel's scale about the panel centre - the check is that the top port row lands at 17.24 mm that way against 17.13 mm from fig-0004's band-4, and the bottom row at 31.71 against 31.50.","info-tab":"photo - the green pull-out tab at the bottom right of the front face (414.5-431.4 x 40.6-42.5) is present in fig-0004, fig-0012 and all three stock photographs. Neither document names it; it is drawn as the library's common/pull-tab because that is what it is, and its function is not claimed.","lifecycle":"searched and found nothing. One web search, 'Edgecore DCS510 AS9716-32D end of life end of sale announcement' (2026-08-28), returned Edgecore's 2020 Q4 and 2022 July EOL notices - neither of which names this model - alongside a live product page and a datasheet revision R11 dated July 2026. So `eol: none-announced` here means the vendor has announced nothing, not that nobody looked.","management-cluster":"measured off dcs510-qsg/fig-0004 at 14x with the figure's own scales, and corroborated in dcs510-qsg/fig-0012 which labels it. The 1000BASE-T mgmt RJ-45 and the USB-A share ONE silver shell - a combined jack, which is why the RJ-45 reads 10.5 mm tall against the console jack's 14.4 mm below it - at x 391.1-407.1, the RJ-45 opening ending at 14.0 and the blue USB tongue at 15.4-21.1. Console RJ-45 388.9-406.7 x 26.2-40.6. The two SFP+ cages 409.4-424.9, at 11.4-22.7 and 26.6-36.1. The legend row 'Mgmt (up)(down) Console' and '10G Mgmt' sits at 24.6, on the same baseline as the port numerals.","panel-decor":"measured - the vent fields. Left column 2.2-5.5 x 6.6-39.2 and right column 432-437.5 full height (dcs510-qsg/fig-0004 dark-cell map); the two horizontal bands across the port field are fig-0004's band-1 and band-2 above (dark centres 2.76 and 7.74) and the field below band-7 (light centre 37.57). The silver shell behind the combined mgmt RJ-45/USB jack is decor rather than a part because it is the jack's own shielding shell, not a separate orderable thing; the four small dark rectangles under the lower SFP+ cage (410.5-422.7 x 37.9-39.5) are drawn as decor for the same reason - they are punched trim, and nothing in either document names them.","port-led-cutouts":"NOT punched, deliberately. common/qsfp-lane-leds-column@1 declares FOUR openings, so expand.py refuses to derive one hole for it - deriving from the body would punch a 1.8 x 11.4 slot and claim the metal has a slot where it has four windows, which no image held here resolves at 3.3 px/mm. L39 stands on all 32 lamps and standing is the correct outcome until somebody reads the metal on a real unit.","port-led-offset":"each lamp column is CENTRED on its port - dy = (10.0 - 11.4) / 2 = -0.70 on both rows - and that is a decision taken AGAINST the measurement, recorded here so the next reader can overturn it with a caliper rather than re-deriving it. What the figures show is a lamp block spaced WIDER row to row than the cages: in dcs510-qsg/fig-0004 the four lamps of the top row read 11.60, 14.65, 17.68, 20.72 mm and the bottom row 27.63, 30.66, 33.71, 36.75, so the two columns sit 16.03 mm apart belly to belly against the port rows' 14.1-14.4, and the same spread appears in dcs510-datasheet/fig-0007 (top row 11.54, 14.47, 17.55, 20.63). It is symmetric - the lamp block and the port block share a centre to 0.2 mm - so it is a spread and not a shift. Drawn on that reading, every lamp column sat 1.0 mm off its own port and L61 said so 32 times, which is the same defect a reviewer found by eye on an earlier model of this device at 1.35 mm. The reading is not strong enough to defend against that. The port ROW PITCH itself reads 13.81 mm from the openings' top edges, 14.37 from their bottom edges and 14.08 from their centres, because this render lights the top lip of every cage and the bottom row is mirrored - so roughly 0.3 mm of the 0.8-1.0 mm offset is the CAGES being measured badly rather than the lamps being placed oddly, and the rest rests on peak-finding at 1.8 px/mm. What would settle it is a straight-on photograph of one shell at better than 3.3 px/mm.","port-leds":"measured - four lamps per port on a 3.0 mm vertical pitch, in a column beside the cage rather than above it. The columns BRACKET each 2-wide shell: the odd column's lamps sit outside it to the left, the even column's outside to the right, which is why the offsets are a per-column list. Read at x 266-277 / y 164,174,184,194 px in dcs510-datasheet/fig-0007 (port 3-4 shell) and independently at x 709-712 / y 51,56.5,62,67 px in dcs510-qsg/fig-0004 (port 31-32 shell); the two agree to 0.15 mm on the pitch. The columns are pushed AWAY from the numeral baseline - the top row's column centres 1.05 mm above its port centre, the bottom row's 1.0 mm below - and that asymmetry is measured, not assumed. Confirmed by eye in dcs510-qsg/fig-0011, which draws eight lamps per shell boundary in two sub-columns.","port-numbering":"drawing - the faceplate prints `n (up)(down) n+1` on ONE baseline between the rows, so odd ports are the TOP row and even the bottom, numbered along: '1 (up)(down) 2' under column 1 and '31 (up)(down) 32' under column 16, read directly in dcs510-qsg/fig-0011 (which resolves 19/20, 21/22, 23/24, 25/26) and dcs510-qsg/fig-0012 (31/32). Numeral offsets +/-2.6 mm from the column centre, from fig-0011 at 5.13 px/mm derived from its own 2-cage shell.","port-numeral-baseline":"measured - fig-0004 band-5, the light band at 24.31 mm between the two dark port rows, is the printing band; the glyphs themselves read 23.8-25.4 mm in the same figure's right-hand block, which puts the baseline at 25.2 and the arrow pair's centre at 24.5.","port-positions":"measured - 16 columns of two. Column centres read off the dark port runs in dcs510-datasheet/fig-0007 panel 0 at 3.2892 px/mm: 47.73, 68.25, 91.81, 112.03, 135.90, 155.81, 179.83, (195.03 clipped), 223.77, 243.07, 267.85, 287.00, 311.47, 331.39, 355.25, 375.17 mm. The seven GROUP pitches (first column of each 2-wide shell to the next) are 44.08, 44.09, 43.93, 43.94, 44.08, 43.62, 43.78 - mean 43.93, spread 0.17 - and the eight within-shell steps average 19.85. The within-shell pitch modelled is the REGISTRY's 19.0 (spec/schemas/standards.yaml qsfp-dd states no pitch key, so w IS the pitch and instances abut), not the 19.85 measured, per the rule that a ganged pitch is a lookup; the gutter was then solved so the LAST column lands where it was measured - 8x19.0 + 7x(19.0+gutter) = 327.44 gives gutter 6.06 - which keeps the far end of the face exact and absorbs the 0.85 mm/shell difference inside each shell, where it is invisible. Row centres 17.13 and 31.50 mm are fig-0004 band-4 and band-6 of the prepared band report (panel box [4,30,803,108], 1.8097 px/mm); row-pitch 14.37.","power":"datasheet - '1300 Watts maximum' for the chassis (dcs510-qsg/doc.md:250, under 'Power Consumption' in the Switch Chassis block, so it is DRAW and not supply). The vendor does not qualify it further and states no typical, and states no ambient, so it is recorded as power-max-w with the envelope unstated. The PSU rating, 1300 W each, is a different number on the other side of the meter and lives on common/psu-ac-1300@1.","rear-ground-points":"drawing - callout 13 of dcs510-datasheet/fig-0007 names a grounding point at each bottom corner of the rear face, and dcs510-qsg's FRU list item 7 says '2 x grounding screws' (doc.md:74). The left one reads at 7.9 mm centre, under the PSU's release latch; it is drawn at 4.5 so that it does not overlap the PSU bay, and the PSU bay starts 2.9 mm right of where the latch reads. Both deviations are the same trade and neither exceeds 3 mm.","rear-layout":"measured - PSU, six fans, PSU. The bright module/chassis boundaries in dcs510-datasheet/fig-0007 panel 1 (3.2801 px/mm) fall at 65.4 and 371.5 mm, and the fan grilles repeat on a 48.8 mm pitch from 76.2 (left edges 76.2, 125.0, 173.8 read at 3x). The face is drawn as an exact mirror about 219.2: PSU bays 9.0-66.0 and 372.4-429.4, grounding points 1.0-8.0 and 430.4-437.4, six fan bays of the library's 48.6 mm generic on the measured 48.8 pitch, centred in the span between the supplies. Fans are numbered 6 to 1 LEFT TO RIGHT, printed between the trays - the same order as the sibling AS7726-32X - read in dcs510-datasheet/fig-0007 and dcs510-qsg/fig-0009. PS2 is the left supply and PS1 the right, printed on the chassis strip beside each with a left-pointing airflow arrow above.","sfp-mgmt-leds":"measured - one lamp per SFP+ port, printed as a row `(lamp) (up)(down) (lamp)` ABOVE the top cage at y 9.3 mm, lamps at 413.5 and 420.2 mm (dcs510-qsg/fig-0004 at 14x). The up/down pair is the same convention the port numerals use, so the left lamp belongs to the upper cage. Semantics from dcs510-qsg/doc.md:100-102, 'SFP+ 10G Mgmt LEDs: Green (10G) Amber (1G)'.","sources":"Two documents, both in working/intake/edgecore/converted. dcs510-datasheet (the DCS510 / AS9716-32D data sheet) carries the spec table, the ordering matrix and fig-0007, a stacked front-and-rear elevation with thirteen callouts. dcs510-qsg (the AS9716-32D quick start guide) carries fig-0004 (front elevation), fig-0009 (rear elevation), fig-0005 (system-LED zoom), fig-0011 (port-LED zoom) and fig-0012 (management-cluster zoom), plus the hardware-specification and LED tables. Three vendor stock photographs (photos/dcs510-1..3) confirm colour and construction only. Both documents letter the artwork AS9716-32D, which is this device's own vendor alias, so the figure/product check the prepared brief asks for passes: the pictures are of the product the text describes.","system-leds":"drawing - Loc, Diag, Fan, PS1, PS2 top to bottom with the Reset pinhole below, read in dcs510-qsg/fig-0005 (the system-LED zoom, which labels every one) and positioned off dcs510-datasheet/fig-0007 at x 116-121 px (33.60 mm) on a 3.23 mm pitch: 7.70, 10.93, 14.16, 17.39, 20.63, Reset at 23.86. The LED semantics are the quick-start's own list, 'PS1/PS2: Green (OK), Amber (fault) / Diag: Green (OK), Amber (no OS or fault) / Fan: Green (OK), Amber (fault) / Loc: Flashing Amber (switch locator)' (dcs510-qsg/doc.md:36-52).","timing-block":"measured - four SMA jacks in a 2x2. Column centres 16.4 and 25.7 mm from the gold-nut mask in dcs510-datasheet/fig-0007 (x clusters 49-76 and 78-107 px); row centres 10.50 and 18.79 mm from dcs510-qsg/fig-0004 (gold rows 44-54 and 59-69). The measured pitches are 9.3 x 8.3 mm and the drawn nut envelope of common/sma-jack@1 is 9.5 across flats, which cannot fit them: the block is drawn on the part's own 9.5 pitch about the measured block centre (21.05, 14.64), so each jack sits 0.6 mm from where it was read. That is the honest version of a nut envelope taken from a different vendor's drawing meeting a jack this figure measures at 8.6 mm; a caliper on the real part settles it.","views":"six views. Front and rear are modelled from the elevations above. Top, bottom, left and right are sized from the datasheet triple and carry only what a photograph of a closed 1RU lid can support: the top's lid seam and rear vent strip and the sides' rail lines are ESTIMATED from the stock three-quarter photograph (photos/dcs510-1) and are marked as such.
